title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Novel Role of Microglia in Fibrovascular Membrane of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: In this study, we used single-cell RNA sequencing on surgically harvested PDR-FVMs and generated a comprehensive cell atlas of FVM.
evidence_context.limitation: Abstract-only evidence (full_text_available=0, OA_fail/no PMCID): claims limited to what the abstract states; sample n and exact cell counts not auditable at claim level.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Novel Role of Microglia in Fibrovascular Membrane of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Eight cellular compositions were identified, with microglia as the major cell population.
evidence_context.limitation: "Major cell population" is per this paper's own annotation of FVM dissociates; independent datasets disagree on microglial vs macrophage identity (cf. D0C-011 refutes-annotation); PDR-only denominator not given in abstract.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Novel Role of Microglia in Fibrovascular Membrane of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: We identified a GPNMB+ subpopulation of microglia, which presented both profibrotic and fibrogenic properties.
evidence_context.limitation: Abstract-level statement; GPNMB+ state attribution to "microglia" (vs monocyte-derived macrophage) is this paper's annotation choice, contested by other D0 papers.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Novel Role of Microglia in Fibrovascular Membrane of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Pseudotime analysis further revealed the profibrotic microglia was uniquely differentiated from retina-resident microglia and expanded in the PDR setting.
evidence_context.limitation: Pseudotime inference from scRNA-seq only — no lineage tracing; trajectory direction not provable from snapshot data; abstract-only source.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Novel Role of Microglia in Fibrovascular Membrane of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Ligand-receptor interactions between the profibrotic microglia and cytokines upregulated in PDR vitreous implicated the involvement of several pathways, including CCR5, IFNGR1, and CD44 signaling, in the microglial activation within the PDR microenvironment.
evidence_context.limitation: Pathway list (CCR5/IFNGR1/CD44) is inferred ligand-receptor analysis on vitreous cytokines, not experimentally validated in the abstract; abstract-only source.

title: Single-cell atlas of the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility in the human retina.

evidence_context.verbatim: We compiled around 3.9 million cells from 125 donors of diverse ancestral backgrounds, including 8 published studies and 2.7 million unpublished data points, to create a comprehensive human retina cell atlas (HRCA) with more than 130 cell types identified.
evidence_context.limitation: Abstract-only evidence; atlas is multistudy (8 published + unpublished 2.7M cells) so per-donor composition of any query cluster is not uniform; OA_fail deviation registered in d0_admission.json.

title: Single-cell atlas of the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility in the human retina.

evidence_context.verbatim: We annotated each cluster, identified marker genes and characterized cis-regulatory elements and gene regulatory networks.
evidence_context.limitation: Marker/regulatory annotation is atlas-level consensus; low-support cell types (e.g. rare immune states) inherit batch/annotation uncertainty; abstract-only source.

title: Single-cell atlas of the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility in the human retina.

evidence_context.verbatim: We modeled changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility across age, ancestry and tissue region.
evidence_context.limitation: Covariate modeling stated in abstract without effect sizes; "tissue region" is macula/peripheral-like axis, not disease state; abstract-only source.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics analysis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy fibrovascular membranes reveals AEBP1 as fibrogenesis modulator.

evidence_context.verbatim: As reported in the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP), we identified 6 different clusters ( Figure 1A ).
evidence_context.limitation: n=4 patient samples, single surgical series (GSE245561); cluster count differs from GSE165784 re-analyses (16-17 clusters) — resolution/division-of-work differences.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics analysis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy fibrovascular membranes reveals AEBP1 as fibrogenesis modulator.

evidence_context.section: Results > Identifying the pericyte cluster within the stromal cells and defining their role in fibrogenesis.
evidence_context.verbatim: Interestingly, we identified an intermediate cluster between pericytes and myofibroblasts, which expressed genes overlapping with both cell types, suggesting that cells within this cluster were transitioning from their pericyte origin toward a myofibroblastic identity ( Figure 6C ).
evidence_context.limitation: Transdifferentiation inferred from clustering/trajectory, not lineage tracing; AEBP1 functional validation is in vitro HRP cells, not membrane tissue.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics analysis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy fibrovascular membranes reveals AEBP1 as fibrogenesis modulator.

evidence_context.verbatim: none of the inflammatory cells expressed microglia markers, such as  TMEM119  and  P2RY12 , in contrast to recent work that claimed microglial population as a main cell type involved in the fibrovascular membrane formation in PDR, with a subpopulation of microglia presenting fibrogenic properties ( 42 ).
evidence_context.limitation: Absence-of-evidence on TMEM119/P2RY12 in their own 4-sample dataset (homeostatic microglia markers can be lost upon activation/dissociation); refutes the microglial *identity* label, not the myeloid-dominant composition itself.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics analysis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy fibrovascular membranes reveals AEBP1 as fibrogenesis modulator.

evidence_context.verbatim: Among the immune cells, we identified a cluster of macrophages,  SPP1 +  cells, expressing a host of proangiogenetic genes, therefore potentially contributing to and exacerbating the angiogenetic environment ( 41 ).
evidence_context.limitation: SPP1+ macrophage subcluster quantified per their own annotation; "proangiogenetic" is gene-expression-inferred, no functional angiogenesis assay for this exact cluster in the cited passage.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics analysis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy fibrovascular membranes reveals AEBP1 as fibrogenesis modulator.

evidence_context.verbatim: scRNA-Seq data are uploaded to NCBI GEO database under accession no.  GSE245561
evidence_context.limitation: Data anchor provenance record only (GSE245561); this card's A-grade composition numbers do NOT use GSE245561.

title: Liquid Biopsy for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Single-Cell Transcriptomics of Human Vitreous Reveals Inflammatory T-Cell Signature.

evidence_context.verbatim: Most vitreous cells were T cells (91.6%), unlike the peripheral blood (46.2%), whereas neutrophils in the vitreous were essentially absent.
evidence_context.limitation: Compartment = cell suspension from cassette washings of vitreous LIQUID (n=5 patients/6 eyes), not digested fibrovascular membrane — T-cell dominance qualifies but does not contradict FVM myeloid-dominance (different compartments).

title: Liquid Biopsy for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Single-Cell Transcriptomics of Human Vitreous Reveals Inflammatory T-Cell Signature.

evidence_context.section: Results > scRNA-seq Resolution of 4 Cell Types in the PDR Vitreous and Peripheral Blood
evidence_context.verbatim: Clustering revealed 4 cell states: T cells, B cells, myeloid, and neutrophils
evidence_context.limitation: Only 4 broad states after QC (13,675 cells); B/neutrophil subclusters too sparse for subtype analysis in some eyes, per the paper.

title: Liquid Biopsy for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Single-Cell Transcriptomics of Human Vitreous Reveals Inflammatory T-Cell Signature.

evidence_context.section: Results > Immune Cell–Cell Interactions within the PDR Vitreous and Peripheral Blood
evidence_context.verbatim: Specifically, interactions between myeloid cells and T cells or dendritic cells (DCs) seem to predominate in the PDR vitreous ( Fig 6 A), whereas myeloid cell subtype interactions such as macrophage–cDC, monocyte–macrophage, and macrophage–macrophage interactions are enriched in both compartments ( Fig 6 A, B).
evidence_context.limitation: Ligand-receptor inference (Dimer Signal Receptor Analysis), not experimental perturbation; vitreous-vs-PBMC comparison constrained by n=5 patients.

title: Liquid Biopsy for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Single-Cell Transcriptomics of Human Vitreous Reveals Inflammatory T-Cell Signature.

evidence_context.verbatim: In the first single-cell transcriptomic characterization of human vitreous in a disease state, we show PDR vitreous is primarily composed of T cells, a critical component of adaptive immunity, with activity and proportions distinct from T cells within the peripheral blood, and neutrophils are essentially absent.
evidence_context.limitation: Conclusion-section framing statement; "liquid biopsy" refers to cassette washings, protocol not standardized across centers at time of publication.

title: Liquid Biopsy for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Single-Cell Transcriptomics of Human Vitreous Reveals Inflammatory T-Cell Signature.

evidence_context.verbatim: A total of 5 of the 6 eyes had received ≥1 injection of anti-VEGF, and two thirds were treated with panretinal photocoagulation at some point before surgery.
evidence_context.limitation: Prior anti-VEGF/PRP treatment may reshape immune composition — composition numbers are treatment-confounded (paper's own cohort table).

title: Single-cell analysis identifies MKI67<sup>+</sup> microglia as drivers of neovascularization in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Gene expression matrix data ( GSE165784 ) were obtained from the GEO database ( http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo ) for further analysis [ 18 ].
evidence_context.limitation: Independent re-analysis of GSE165784 confirms 5 FVM samples from PDR patients as the dataset scope; their QC (UMI 200-3000, MT>10%) and cell yield (7,764) differ from our Track B (10,069 cells) — anchor to dataset identity, not to numbers.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies MKI67<sup>+</sup> microglia as drivers of neovascularization in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Stringent quality control measures were applied to exclude low-quality cells, defined as those with unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts below 200 or above 3000, as well as cells exhibiting mitochondrial gene expression greater than 10%.
evidence_context.limitation: Third-party QC recipe for GSE165784 (UMI bounds + MT filter) — method anchor for sensitivity checks only; not adopted by Track B.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies MKI67<sup>+</sup> microglia as drivers of neovascularization in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: this investigation is the first to delineate a novel microglial subset, designated as MKI67 +  microglia, distinguished by robust upregulation of genes implicated in lactate metabolic processes and proliferation, such as MKI67, PARK7 and LDHA
evidence_context.limitation: "Microglia" label here is marker-based on GSE165784 re-analysis; subset defined post-hoc via LMG intersection; proliferation (MKI67) signature could also reflect infiltrating myeloid cycling cells.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies MKI67<sup>+</sup> microglia as drivers of neovascularization in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

evidence_context.section: Results > scRNA-seq data integration and clustering of fibrovascular membrane
evidence_context.verbatim: microglial cells (markers: CENPF, CX3CR1, SELENOP, HIST1H1B, GPNMB, FABP5, MRC1, and LIPA)
evidence_context.limitation: Their microglia marker panel (SELENOP/MRC1/GPNMB...) overlaps heavily with states our Track B annotates as macrophage — evidences that MG-vs-Mac annotation in FVM is panel-dependent, not data-determined.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies MKI67<sup>+</sup> microglia as drivers of neovascularization in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: This unique cell type promotes angiogenesis by interacting with endothelial cells via secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1)-Integrin alpha 4 (ITGA4) signaling.
evidence_context.limitation: SPP1-ITGA4 pair from CellPhoneDB inference + conditioned-medium co-culture (in vitro); mouse OIR arm supports drug effect, not the human cell state directly.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies MKI67<sup>+</sup> microglia as drivers of neovascularization in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: In the in vivo OIR model, treatment with abemaciclib, a FDA-approved proliferation inhibitor, significantly reduced neovascularization.
evidence_context.limitation: Mouse OIR model (P12-P17 i.p. abemaciclib), not PDR human tissue; translational gap acknowledged — no human efficacy data in this paper.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of the neovascular niche promotes regenerative angiogenesis in proliferative retinopathy.

evidence_context.section: Results > Fatty-acid oxidation is a metabolic hallmark of pathological angiogenesis
evidence_context.verbatim: we observed an accumulation of acylcarnitines in human neovascular PR samples compared to control subjects with epiretinal membranes
evidence_context.limitation: Human evidence = vitreous metabolomics (PDR vs ERM controls, pre-2017 collection, n per Suppl Table 1); acylcarnitine accumulation is niche-level, not cell-type-resolved.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of the neovascular niche promotes regenerative angiogenesis in proliferative retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Neovascular tufts with a distinct single-cell transcriptional signature highly expressed FAO enzymes.
evidence_context.limitation: Tuft EC signature from mouse OIR CD31-enriched Drop-seq (GSE216676), not human FVM endothelium — cross-species transfer is this paper's hypothesis, supported only by the metabolite match (D0C-028).

title: Metabolic reprogramming of the neovascular niche promotes regenerative angiogenesis in proliferative retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: The deletion of  Sirt3 , an FAO regulator, shifted the neovascular niche metabolism from FAO to glycolysis and suppressed tuft formation.
evidence_context.limitation: Global Sirt3-/- mouse (also AAV-GFAP-Cre conditional arm); mechanism is niche-level metabolic reprogramming — tuft suppression shown in OIR, not in diabetic human retina.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of the neovascular niche promotes regenerative angiogenesis in proliferative retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Interestingly, we observed comparable FAO metabolite signatures in both human diabetic PR and murine OIR samples, suggesting a shared metabolic dysregulation in neovascular disease despite their distinct etiologies.
evidence_context.limitation: Discussion-level comparison of metabolite classes; "shared metabolic dysregulation" remains associative (different etiologies, different readouts: human vitreous vs mouse retinal acylcarnitines).

title: Metabolic reprogramming of the neovascular niche promotes regenerative angiogenesis in proliferative retinopathy.

evidence_context.verbatim: Poor glucose control in diabetics and extreme prematurity in neonates correlate with neovascular retinal disease in humans but not in mice.
evidence_context.limitation: Paper's own model-limitation admission — applies to all OIR-derived claims used for human PDR inference (incl. D0C-026/027).

title: Human single-cell atlas of proliferative diabetic retinopathy reveals a SOX15-overexpressing stromal population driving retinal fibrosis through the endothelin-

evidence_context.verbatim: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on primary retinal tissues from PDR organ donors and non-diabetic controls, generating a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human PDR retina.
evidence_context.limitation: Atlas scope = post-mortem donor RETINA tissue (2 PDR donors/4 retinas + 3 controls/6 retinas), a different compartment from surgically harvested FVM; FVM only used in IF validation arms.

title: Human single-cell atlas of proliferative diabetic retinopathy reveals a SOX15-overexpressing stromal population driving retinal fibrosis through the endothelin-

evidence_context.verbatim: Notably, We identified a stromal cell population that was enriched in PDR retinas, localized in FVMs, and characterized by high SOX15 expression.
evidence_context.limitation: SOX15-high stromal subpopulation defined in their own PDR retinal atlas (n=2 PDR donors; 80.6% of stromal cells from one donor PDR2 per their Fig.); FVM localization by IF on 3 samples.

title: Human single-cell atlas of proliferative diabetic retinopathy reveals a SOX15-overexpressing stromal population driving retinal fibrosis through the endothelin-

evidence_context.verbatim: Mechanistically, SOX15 regulates EDN1 transcription through binding to its promoter, driving EDN1 expression that activates EDNRB-expressing retinal macroglia to promote reactive gliosis and retinal fibrosis.
evidence_context.limitation: Mechanism chain: ChIP-seq/qPCR + luciferase (in vitro/overexpression) + Sox15-dFIB mouse laser-fibrosis model; human evidence is correlative at tissue level.

title: Human single-cell atlas of proliferative diabetic retinopathy reveals a SOX15-overexpressing stromal population driving retinal fibrosis through the endothelin-

evidence_context.verbatim: It is also worth noting that prior scRNA-seq studies of PDR have focused on FVM tissues surgically retrieved during vitrectomy.
evidence_context.limitation: Explicit compartment distinction from Discussion — supports treating FVM-derived composition priors as membrane-scope, not retina-scope.

title: Human single-cell atlas of proliferative diabetic retinopathy reveals a SOX15-overexpressing stromal population driving retinal fibrosis through the endothelin-

evidence_context.verbatim: One landmark study identified eight cellular populations in FVMs with microglia as the dominant cell type, and found mesenchymal lineage accounting for 8.2% [ 14 ].
evidence_context.limitation: Third-party recount of Hu 2022 (GSE165784): "microglia dominant" and mesenchymal 8.2% are as-annotated by that study — quoted here as provenance context, not independently re-derived.

title: Human single-cell atlas of proliferative diabetic retinopathy reveals a SOX15-overexpressing stromal population driving retinal fibrosis through the endothelin-

evidence_context.verbatim: First, the absence of non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) samples in our scRNA-seq cohort represents a missed opportunity to characterize the transcriptomic transition from non-proliferative to proliferative disease and to identify early cellular markers preceding FVM formation.
evidence_context.limitation: Self-declared limitation: disease-stage gradient (NPDR->PDR) not covered by their atlas; photoreceptor subpopulation claims (MT-enriched rods, S-cones loss) rest on n=2 PDR donors.
